clue.text: In the Pyrenees he's said to lie in the sun

indicators.note: said to tells us the word for sunbathing is only heard, its spelling differs

parts.note: to lie in the sun is to bask

explanation.surface: A man somewhere in the mountains between France and Spain is supposedly sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Basques are a people living in the western Pyrenees, either side of the French-Spanish border.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the people native to the western Pyrenees region is a member of that ethnic group.

clue.text: Pompous old boy upset adhesive, swamping front of book

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the old boy abbreviation is turned over

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: swamping means the glue word engulfs the book's opening letter

parts.note: mastic is a resin used as an adhesive

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of book

explanation.surface: A self-important former pupil knocks over glue that floods a book cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OB into BO; 'swamping' puts B inside MASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflated, high-sounding language is pompous.

clue.text: Like sodium chlorate, this clue is!

explanation.surface: A comment that the clue is like a chemical salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Sodium chlorate dissolves in water; the clue itself can be worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt dissolves in liquid, and a puzzle that can be worked out has the same adjective.

clue.text: Peacekeepers have quarters, practicable though not desirable

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces
E and N are two compass quarters, east and north
viable means practicable, workable

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping troops have living quarters that are workable but unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody would envy is undesirable.

clue.text: A wartime hero's alternative name for General Grant

definitions.text: A wartime hero's alternative name for General Grant

parts.words: A wartime hero's alternative name for General Grant
parts.note: Grant's first name was Ulysses, the Latin form of the Greek name of the Trojan War hero who sailed home to Ithaca

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a nickname for the American Civil War general.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant shares his first name with the Roman form of the Greek hero of the Trojan War; the Greek form is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's wily Greek hero of the Trojan War is called Ulysses in Latin, General Grant's first name.

clue.text: Dig up bed in most peculiar way

indicators.note: in a peculiar way means the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone digs over a garden bed in a strange manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar way' rearranges the letters of BED IN MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a body out of a tomb is to exhume, to dig it up.

clue.text: Lively schoolboy's starting to snoop

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of schoolboy's

parts.note: to pry is to snoop

explanation.surface: An energetic boy begins spying.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and energetic, especially of an older person.

clue.text: He hopes to have the choice at the top

definitions.text: He hopes to have the choice at the top

parts.words: He hopes to have the choice at the top
parts.note: choice here is the noun for the select few, the elite, which such a person wants in charge

explanation.surface: Someone wants to pick what happens at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choice' reads as an option but means the best people, the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes a select few should rule wants the best people in power.

clue.text: A sword for poets to lift, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for lift is heard, spelt differently

parts.note: to lift is to steal

explanation.surface: Poets reach for a sword to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a blade is often called by the metal it is made from.

clue.text: Spring finds us in good health

explanation.surface: A spa spring keeps us fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of water from the ground, and an adjective for being healthy.

clue.text: European man carrying educational journal

indicators.note: carrying means the word for man holds the journal inside it

parts.note: a man is a male
TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' paper

explanation.surface: A man is seen holding a copy of a teaching magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES (Times Educational Supplement) is the British weekly paper for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the island nation of Malta in the Mediterranean is a European.

clue.text: A stone of fish

explanation.surface: Someone weighs fourteen pounds of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, which is the misdirection; sardine is also an old name for a gemstone, the sard or sardius.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardine-stone is a biblical name for a reddish gem (sard), and the word is also a small oily fish of the herring family.

clue.text: In two minds about broadcasting "Batman" live

indicators.note: about and broadcasting both suggest the letters of these words being scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is undecided about airing a live Batman show.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in two minds means having mixed or conflicting feelings, undecided.

clue.text: Vessel coming through entrance to lock

parts.note: via means by way of, coming through

indicators.note: entrance to means the opening letter of lock

explanation.surface: A boat passes through the gate of a canal lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass bottle for medicine or perfume is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Quiet nobleman Verdi represented as a collector of gems

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: represented means the letters of Verdi are presented anew in another order

explanation.surface: A quiet aristocrat plays Verdi like a gem collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer who goes under the sea bringing up oysters gathers precious gems.

clue.text: Ensnares and beats up captured agent

indicators.note: captured means the word for beats up holds the agent inside it

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them up
a rep is a sales representative, an agent

explanation.surface: Someone traps and assaults a captured spy.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan is an old verb meaning to trap or lure someone into a snare.

clue.text: Thus Pliny's first chronicle, lacking nothing in fallacious reasoning

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Pliny's
lacking means the chronicle word loses a letter

parts.note: a history is a chronicle
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The Roman writer's chronicle is full of bad logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever but deceptive argument meant to mislead is fallacious reasoning.

clue.text: Enough for Cardinal Newman, this dance?

explanation.surface: A question about a ballroom step Newman would have found sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: Newman's hymn 'Lead, Kindly Light' has the line 'one step enough for me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newman's hymn asks for a single pace forward, no more; it is also a quick ragtime-era ballroom dance.

clue.text: By arresting one member, girl almost identifies the plant

indicators.note: arresting means the word for by holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: almost means the girl's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Nell is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl spots a flower after one member is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' puts I and MP inside PER; 'almost' cuts NELL to NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small red-flowered plant of the primrose family.

clue.text: It grows when rudeness initially intimidates

indicators.note: initially means the word for intimidates comes at the start, before the cheek

parts.note: cows means frightens or intimidates
lip is cheeky talk, rudeness

explanation.surface: A general remark about bullying getting worse when insolence comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow spring wildflower is a plant, something that grows.

clue.text: Keen to catch a great bird

indicators.note: to catch means the cry word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief
GT is short for great

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to spot a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bird that bobs its long tail up and down.

clue.text: Being wearied, rode foolishly into retreating crowd

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters go inside the turned-round crowd
retreating means the crowd word is read backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of rode are muddled

explanation.surface: A tired rider charges stupidly into a mob that falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' makes ORED from rode; 'retreating' turns MOB into BOM, and 'into' puts ORED inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui, the state of being wearied by dullness, is a synonym.

clue.text: Our sole cleaner — a downtrodden person

explanation.surface: The only person who cleans for us is badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as only but means the bottom of a shoe, wiped on a mat at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat wipes the bottoms of shoes, and someone others walk all over is a pushover.

clue.text: About to grow old in prison

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone is approaching old age behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A barred enclosure for confining animals or people is a prison.

clue.text: Round door fastener

explanation.surface: A round knob that latches a door.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is a song for several voices entering in turn; a comic one is a canon of that kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A round for singers of the comic kind, and a latch holding a door shut.

clue.text: Pop rode him recklessly in the circus

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters of these three words are thrown around

explanation.surface: Dad rode the man wildly at the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece and Rome the arena for horse and chariot races was a circus; later the name of variety theatres.

clue.text: Old northerner caught in trap

indicators.note: in means the cricket letter goes inside the trap word

parts.note: a pit is a trap for animals
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot is captured in a pitfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient people of northern Scotland are old northerners.

clue.text: The sort to incite the French to leave

indicators.note: to leave means the French article is taken out of the incite word

parts.note: to kindle is to stir up or incite
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to make the French depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind means type or sort, as in 'of this nature'.

clue.text: Way to back a king? It's novel for an absolutist

indicators.note: to back means the abbreviation for way is turned round

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: novel means fresh or new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporting a monarch, says a book, marks you out as an autocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns ST into TS; 'novel' rearranges ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the Russian emperors' autocratic rule is an absolutist.

clue.text: Primitive types of church people accepting the King James Bible

indicators.note: accepting means the church and people words take the Bible abbreviation inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
AV is the Authorized Version, the King James Bible
men means people

explanation.surface: Churchgoers who welcome the 1611 translation are dismissed as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The King James Bible is known in Britain as the Authorized Version, AV.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone Age people living in rock shelters are the archetypal primitive types.

clue.text: Eg Billie's periods of recreation

explanation.surface: A note that jazz singer Billie's are times for leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: Billie Holiday was an American jazz singer, so something belonging to her is her surname plus 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie the jazz singer's surname with a possessive, and also times of rest from work, vacations.

clue.text: Rejected in school, a turbulent boy becomes ruthless

indicators.note: Rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie within the words school, a turbulent

explanation.surface: A troubled boy expelled from school turns cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'boy becomes ruthless' as the definition, but only 'ruthless' defines; 'boy becomes' is surface. 'in' marks the run LATURB, which 'Rejected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel and savage behaviour, showing no mercy, is a synonym of ruthless.
